anya: Quick heads-up — saw headwise saturation spikes on the fp8 canary for customer A (longctx). ~0.6% tokens with abs(scale) > 1200 and a couple heads hitting overflow. Not catastrophic but quality regressions in rarely used prompts.

jason: Ugh, that sounds like the headwise scale drift we simulated. Can you paste the per-head stats snapshot?

anya: Sure — pasting the trimmed log:
```
layer: 21, head: 3, max_abs_scale: 1624, p95_abs_scale: 420
layer: 21, head: 7, max_abs_scale: 1198, p95_abs_scale: 390
layer: 48, head: 11, max_abs_scale: 1320, p95_abs_scale: 470
Total tokens sampled: 125k, tokens_over_1024: 762 (0.61%)
```

lee: Thanks. Runtime / perf note: adding headwise clipping will require a different kernel or an extra post-scale pass. On our 80GB cards that could add ~0.5–0.8ms p90 for longctx flows. We should weigh latency cost vs quality benefit.

kazu: Proposal for experiments: 1) bucketize high-scale heads into a "saturation" list (per-model), 2) apply conservative clamp cap at 1024 for buckets, 3) if a head exceeds cap persistently, route that layer to int8 (per-layer fallback) for that model version and canary slice. Shadow-eval regen-rate & rouge/perplexity delta.

anya: I like that. Also think we need telemetry changes: add fields (model, layer_idx, head_idx, abs_scale, token_count, customer_id) so we can correlate by tenant and prompt shape.

jason: For the per-layer int8 fallback, runtime must guarantee fast hot-swap. We should reuse the existing precision-adapter interface (opt-in flag at request-level) rather than shipping a brand new code-path. Ops checklist needs a canary-with-rollback plan.

anya: Draft rollout plan: "telemetry + small runtime shim + profile bucketizer + canary". Canary schedule: 1% traffic 24h -> 5% 48h -> 20% 72h, with automatic rollback if regen-rate > 1.5x or human quality alerts. Owners: anya (quant telemetry + RFC), jason (runtime shim + canary), lee (perf measurement).

sre-bot: deploy: quant-telemetry/telemetry-v2 -> staging succeeded (build 2026.03.22-21).

jason: Also add a per-customer override in profile metadata so Dedicated customers can force-fail to int8 if they have hard quality SLAs.

lee: Ack. I'll sketch the shim API:
```json
{"precision_override": "layer_48:int8", "head_clamp_map": [[21,3],[48,11]]}
```
Keep it opt-in by default.

anya: Great — I'll open a short RFC with the experiment matrix, telemetry fields, and ops playbook. Will @product for prioritization and add the canary tickets. :thumbsup:

jason: Thanks — ping me when the RFC lands, I'll wire the adapter into the runtime tests.

kazu: One more ask: include a small offline calibration run in the canary so we can check deterministic regen on historical prompts before enabling traffic.

anya: Will do. Thanks all.
